events.title: ÁLVARO MORENO ABAJO PhD THESIS DEFENSE: Optical investigation of 2D materials with in-plane engineering: exciton confinement and chirality sensing
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: ÁLVARO MORENO ABAJO PhD THESIS DEFENSE: Optical investigation of 2D materials with in-plane engineering: exciton confinement and chirality sensing
events.detail_text: Theses Defenses July 20, 2026 ÁLVARO MORENO ABAJO Hour: 11:00h Place: ICFO Auditorium Share Outlook iCalendar Google PhD THESIS DEFENSE: Optical investigation of 2D materials with in-plane engineering: exciton confinement and chirality sensing ÁLVARO MORENO ABAJO Quantum Nano-Optoelectronics, ICFO Two-dimensional (2D) materials provide a powerful platform for nanoscale engineering and control of geometry and energy landscapes without directly modifying the material, owing to their interfacial nature. This thesis explores how we can harness this potential by introducing in-plane engineering in van der Waals heterostructures. We present two case studies: in one, the exciton dimensionality is reduced using a designed 1D electrostatic trap; in the other, twisting two monolayers yields a chiral configuration that modifies the interaction with other chiral systems. Together, these two parts demonstrate how inplane symmetry breaking (translational and mirror symmetry, respectively) in 2D material platforms enables new modalities of control and sensing. In the first part, we investigate electrostatically defined confinement of intralayer excitons in MoSe2. A p–i–n junction is induced in the monolayer by asymmetric gating, creating a tight 1D potential with an effective exciton confinement length down to 10nm. events.title: Extrasolar planets with gravitational microlensing and the Earth 2.0 mission
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: Extrasolar planets with gravitational microlensing and the Earth 2.0 mission
events.venue: DAM 7.24 Seminar Room and via Zoom
events.detail_text: Abstract : Microlensing has emerged as a powerful technique for discovering cold extrasolar planets beyond the snowline, as well as free-floating planets. In this talk, I will begin by explaining the basic principles of gravitational microlensing, then review recent findings from ongoing surveys, and finally explore the discoveries anticipated from the upcoming Earth 2.0 mission satellite and Roman Space Telescope.

events.title: ALBA CALATAYUD NANOFABRICATION SEMINAR: Not so nano anymore: Bridging Cleanroom Tools and Biological Systems
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: ALBA CALATAYUD NANOFABRICATION SEMINAR: Not so nano anymore: Bridging Cleanroom Tools and Biological Systems
events.speakers: Not so nano anymore: Bridging Cleanroom Tools and Biological Systems
events.detail_text: Seminars July 22, 2026 ALBA CALATAYUD NANOFABRICATION SEMINAR: Not so nano anymore: Bridging Cleanroom Tools and Biological Systems Hour: From 12:00h to 13:00h Place: Seminar Room Share Outlook iCalendar Google NANOFABRICATION SEMINAR: Not so nano anymore: Bridging Cleanroom Tools and Biological Systems ALBA CALATAYUD Neurophotonics and Mechanical Systems Biology, ICFO In the cleanroom, we are usually focused on achieving smaller features, higher resolution, and increasingly precise control at the nanoscale. But in life sciences, length scales are often in the micron range, where the challenges are different: not just resolution, but large geometries, structural robustness of the molds, and high-aspect-ratio fidelity. In this talk, I will show how standard cleanroom tools such as photolithography and RIE can be used to produce silicon molds from which PDMS microfluidic and micromechanical devices are cast, focusing on the practical limitations that arise when moving from design to real devices. Although PDMS is mainly used for biological research, which is my main focus, it is an almost transparent elastomer that can replicate features down to the nanoscale, opening the door to useful tools for our day-to-day experiments such as directing fluids, holding optical components, or stamping electrodes. Your imagination is the limit! Hosted by NFL Users Seminars July 22, 2026 ALBA CALATAYUD NANOFABRICATION SEMINAR: Not so nano anymore: Bridging Cleanroom Tools and Biological System

events.title: Visita guiada a «Nonell, Vallmitjana i els gitanos» a càrrec de Julià Guillamon
events.label: Amics CCCB
events.summary: Visita guiada a «Nonell, Vallmitjana i els gitanos» a càrrec de Julià Guillamon. Amics CCCB
events.speakers: Julià Guillamon Aquesta activitat forma part de:
events.detail_text: Una visita comentada amb el comissari Julià Guillamon per endinsar-nos en una exposició que explora les relacions artístiques i literàries entre Isidre Nonell i Juli Vallmitjana, i que ens obre una finestra a la Barcelona dels marges del tombant de segle. En Julià Guillamon ens guia per «Nonell, Vallmitjana i els gitanos», una exposició fruit d’un treball de recerca desenvolupat conjuntament amb en Joan Mar Sauqué. La mostra aporta noves claus sobre l’amistat entre el pintor i l’escriptor, així com sobre el context artístic, literari i social en què es van moure. També ressegueix el trencament abrupte de la seva relació cap al 1906 i amplia la mirada cap a altres figures de la seva generació. Al llarg de la visita, aprofundirem en el vincle entre Nonell i Vallmitjana, en la seva mirada sobre els suburbis i la vida als marges de la Barcelona d’aquell moment, i en el paper central que aquestes realitats tenen per entendre una època convulsa però extraordinàriament rica en creativitat. Aquesta visita és, en definitiva, una invitació a descobrir, de la mà del seu comissari, una constel·lació d’obres, vincles i històries que ens apropen a una altra manera de llegir la història cultural de Barcelona: la que es construeix des dels marges, entre tallers, carrers i formes de vida sovint absents del relat oficial.

events.title: Watching Quantum Fields Evolve: Partons and Thermalization on Quantum Computers
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: Watching Quantum Fields Evolve: Partons and Thermalization on Quantum Computers
events.venue: Pere Pascual V5.07 Room and via Zoom
events.detail_text: Abstract : Many of the most important phenomena in quantum field theory—parton dynamics, real-time evolution, and thermalization—are extremely difficult to study with conventional classical computers. Quantum computers provide a new opportunity: they allow us to simulate quantum systems by using another controllable quantum system. In this talk, I will present two recent field-theory calculations carried out on quantum computers, based on arXiv:2506.16829 and arXiv:2603.23948. The first explores parton distributions in the Schwinger model, connecting quantum simulation to the internal structure of relativistic bound states. The second investigates thermalization in SU(2) lattice gauge fields, addressing how apparently thermal behavior can emerge from unitary quantum evolution. No prior knowledge of quantum computing will be assumed; the talk will focus on the physics motivation, the basic ideas, and what these calculations teach us about real-time quantum field theory.

events.title: Continuous operation of a coherent 3,000-qubit system
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: Continuous operation of a coherent 3,000-qubit system
events.detail_text: Abstract : Arrays of neutral atoms have emerged as a powerful platform for quantum computing. One limitation to achieving deep circuit depths is atom loss occuring during gate operations and collisions with the background molecules in an vacuum. In this talk, I will present a new experimental architecture where this atom loss can be compensated by continuously reloading fresh atoms into the atomic array. Our architecture employs a pair of optical conveyor belts that transport dense atomic reservoirs, initially prepared in a first vacuum chamber, into a second chamber where they are positioned near the quantum processor. Importantly, loading new atoms from the reservoir is non-destructive to the quantum state of the nearby array, enabling deep circuits through mid-circuit atom replacement in future experiments. Demonstrating a reloading rate of 300,000 atoms in tweezers per second, we create over 30,000 initialized qubits per second, which we leverage to assemble and maintain an array of over 3,000 atoms for more than two hours. At the end of the talk, I will focus on molecular physics emerging from long-range Rydberg interactions. I will summarize studies of so-called Rydberg macrodimers using quantum gas microscopy and briefly discuss new insights into the interaction blockade between pairs of macrodimers, which can be understood through the Rydberg interactions among all four participating Rydberg atoms.

events.title: Visita guiada a «El culte a la bellesa» amb blanca arias i Júlia Lull Sanz
events.label: Amics CCCB
events.summary: Visita guiada a «El culte a la bellesa» amb blanca arias i Júlia Lull Sanz. Amics CCCB
events.speakers: Júlia Lull Sanz blanca arias Aquesta activitat forma part de:
events.detail_text: blanca arias i Júlia Lull Sanz conduiran una visita guiada exclusiva per a la comunitat d’Amics del CCCB a «El culte a la bellesa», una exposició que examina com s’han configurat els ideals estètics, quins mecanismes els han sostingut al llarg del temps i quins cossos n’han quedat al marge. Aquesta visita ofereix l’oportunitat de recórrer «El culte a la bellesa» a càrrec de les dues comissàries responsables de la seva adaptació al CCCB, a partir d’un projecte presentat inicialment a la Wellcome Collection de Londres. Al llarg del recorregut, blanca arias i Júlia Lull Sanz compartiran les principals línies de lectura de la mostra i situaran algunes de les preguntes que l’articulen: de quina manera els cànons de bellesa s’han construït històricament, quines formes de poder han contribuït a fixar-los i com han condicionat la representació dels cossos. La visita permetrà apropar-se a l’exposició des de la mirada de dues professionals amb una trajectòria sòlida en el camp del pensament visual, el comissariat i la mediació cultural: blanca arias, vinculada a la Fundació Miró i al MACBA, i Júlia Lull Sanz, investigadora i professora de la UPF amb una trajectòria consolidada en projectes feministes i de recerca sobre la imatge. Aquesta proposta convida a entrar en els continguts de la mostra des d’una relació més propera amb les seves comissàries i a compartir una experiència de visita que afavoreix la conversa, l’atenció i l’aprofundiment.

events.title: Visita el Mirador del CCCB 2026
events.venue: Mirador, des de la qual es poden contemplar unes magnífiques vistes de la ciutat de Barcelona. El Mi
events.detail_text: Un diumenge al mes i en algunes dates assenyalades el CCCB obre al públic la Sala Mirador, des de la qual es poden contemplar unes magnífiques vistes de la ciutat de Barcelona. El Mirador, situat a la cinquena planta de l'edifici del CCCB, és un dels espais més emblemàtics del Centre i, a través de la façana de vidre, permet veure Barcelona des d’una perspectiva diferent: el mar, el Raval i Ciutat Vella, Montjuïc, el Tibidabo i la Torre de Collserola.
